description: This institute-core course for Electrical Engineering covers the basics and importance of numerical analysis for analyzing problems that arise in engineering and physical sciences, gives students a deeper knowledge of probability and distributions, studies topics of discrete mathematics with engineering applications, and covers statistical methods and testing of hypotheses.

syllabus.title: Linear and Nonlinear Algebraic Equations
syllabus.body: Numerical solution of algebraic and transcendental equations: Regula-Falsi method and Newton-Raphson method. Solution of linear system of equations: Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel iteration method and convergence (without proof). Calculation of dominant eigenvalue by iteration method.

syllabus.title: Function Approximation
syllabus.body: Introduction to Newton's forward and backward interpolation, Lagrange interpolation, finite differences, numerical integration by Trapezoidal and Simpson's 1/3 rule, Romberg integration and Gaussian quadrature rule.

syllabus.title: Ordinary Differential Equations
syllabus.body: Taylor series method, Picard's method, Euler's method, modified Euler's method, Runge-Kutta method of 2nd and 4th orders, predictor-corrector methods, Milne's method, convergence criteria, finite difference method for boundary value problems.

syllabus.title: Discrete Probability and Statistical Methods
syllabus.body: Definitions, axioms of probability, set theory, probability space, conditional probability, combined experiments, Bernoulli trials, Bernoulli's theorem and games of chance, problems. Large sample tests: procedure of testing hypothesis, small sample tests, Student's T-test, Chi-Square test, independence of attributes and goodness of fit.

outcomes: Give numerical solutions to algebraic and transcendental equations.
Numerically integrate functions of one and two variables.
Provide numerical solutions of ordinary differential equations using one-step and multi-step methods.
Use discrete and continuous probability distributions in practical problems.
Apply different testing tools like Student's T-test, Chi-square test, etc. to analyse relevant real-life problems.

Paras Ram, Engineering Mathematics through Applications, 2nd Edition, CBS Publishers, 2015.
